groups.title: React Component Model
groups.question: You are building the React frontend for your recipe API with a list page, a detail page and a recipe card. Explain how components, state and routing work.

followUps.Components, Props, and Composition: Why are props read-only, and how do you build complex UIs from small parts?
followUps.State Management with useState and useEf: How do useState and useEffect work together to load data?
followUps.Client-Side Routing with React Router: How does React Router show the detail page for /recipes/5 without reloading?

evidence.text: A React UI is a tree of components.
Props are read-only inputs passed from parent to child.
Small focused components are combined to build larger screens.
useState stores local values that trigger a re-render when changed.
useEffect synchronises the component with outside systems like an API.
The dependency array decides when the effect runs again and prevents stale values.
React Router maps URL paths to components.
Navigation changes the view without a full page reload.
useParams reads values like the recipe id from the URL, and useNavigate navigates from code.

groups.title: Forms and Data Fetching
groups.question: You are building a 'new recipe' form and a list that loads recipes from Django. Explain how you would handle form input and fetching.

followUps.Controlled Inputs and Form Handling: What makes an input controlled, and when would you use an uncontrolled one?
followUps.Fetching API Data with useEffect: What states must a component handle when fetching data?

evidence.text: A controlled input's value is held in React state and updated on change.
That makes validation and submission straightforward.
Uncontrolled inputs with refs suit cases like file inputs.

notEnough: Only saying you use value and onChange.

evidence.text: Data is fetched inside an effect with fetch or Axios.
The component shows a loading state while waiting.
Errors are caught and shown to the user.

notEnough: Only saying you fetch in useEffect.

groups.title: Project Structure and Tooling
groups.question: You are setting up the React project and the codebase is getting hard to navigate. Explain your tooling and file organisation.

followUps.Scaffolding with Vite or Create React Ap: Why choose Vite for a new React project?
followUps.Organising a React Codebase: How would you organise files as the app grows?

evidence.text: Vite starts quickly and updates instantly during development.
It serves modules natively in development.
Create React App is older and slower and no longer recommended.
Group files by feature instead of by type.
Keep a component's styles and tests next to it.
An index file per feature can simplify imports.

groups.title: Developer Experience
groups.question: A component shows the wrong data and a teammate keeps forgetting effect dependencies. Explain the tools you would use to debug and prevent this.

followUps.React DevTools Browser Extension: What can you see with React DevTools?
followUps.ESLint and Prettier for React Projects: How do ESLint and Prettier help a React team?

evidence.text: It shows the component tree.
You can inspect each component's props and state.
The profiler shows which components render and how long they take.

notEnough: Only saying it is a browser extension.

evidence.text: The React hooks lint rules catch broken hook rules and missing effect dependencies.
Prettier formats code automatically.
Together they catch bugs early and keep code consistent.
